title: 13 of devbin's 28 built-ins have no authored page anywhere -- 0112 closed on a population devbin's own language declaration narrowed
body:
FOUND by cc's review of 0112 on 2026-09-23, and agreed by vc, who built 0112, as a finding against its close.

0112 closed at 3a4cd53 on "every verb devbin offers now has an authored page". Its arm is documentation.bats's "EVERY command devbin offers in its own tree has authored help" (8a8d1ae). The arm takes its set from the listing `bin/devbin help` prints in DEVBIN'S OWN TREE, with a floor of sixteen. Devbin declares one language, shell, so that listing leaves out every built-in devbin scopes to another language or leaves opt-in. The arm names its population honestly in its title. The close did not, and it read as every built-in.

MEASURED 2026-09-23. Devbin's catalogue has 28 built-ins (`builtin_commands`), and 15 of them have a page: build, check, devbin, docs, doctor, fmt, infra, install, new, release, shell-init, test, upgrade, vendor and version. The other 13 have none anywhere:
- elixir: server, iex, cli, repl and db;
- rust: fullcycle and dormancy;
- opt-in: precommit, content, publish, macos and which;
- clean, which is inactive in devbin's own tree because every option it offers is.

`help --why` was read in all 16 estates on 0.1.7. 8 of the 13 resolve to devbin's own implementation in at least one estate: clean in 10 estates, dormancy in 5, fullcycle 4, iex 4, cli 3, repl 3, db 2 and server 2. In each of those estates, `help <cmd>` prints the stub, which tells the estate to write devbin's page itself.

WHY THIS IS NOT PART OF 0113. 0113 is delivery: getting the pages devbin has to the estates. Its design keeps these 13 honest meanwhile. Its arm 7(f) holds every page-less built-in to a stub that says devbin ships no page for it yet and never says "Write it at", and arms 7(a) and 7(f) together account for all 28. This issue is the content: one page for each of the 13, written from its handler and checked claim by claim against the running code, as 0112's were. Each goes in the shipped format 0113 fixes: `lib/pages/`, prettier-stable, and true in any estate where devbin's implementation of the command runs.

ORDER, if hv wants one: by measured use -- clean, dormancy, fullcycle, iex, cli, repl, db, server -- then the five opt-ins no estate has enabled. When this is built is hv's call.

## Resolution

Fixed at a4c1447. Ships in 0.1.8.

- WHAT CHANGED. Thirteen pages under lib/pages/: clean, cli, content, db, dormancy, fullcycle, iex, macos, precommit, publish, repl, server and which. With the fifteen 0113 moved there, every one of the catalogue's 28 built-ins answers `bin/devbin help <cmd>` with devbin's page and the "In this project:" trailer. help.bats's two floors rise from 15 to 28, and the catalogue arm asserts that every built-in answers with a page.
- HOW THEY WERE WRITTEN. Four page agents against a clean clone of the landing base, each keeping a claims file (the claim, its file:line, the fixture drive, the verdict); cc audited every page against the code and drove every defect the agents reported. 26 of 27 reproduce, filed as 0131-0136 and 0128's amendment; the 27th is by design. Where a filed issue changes behaviour a page describes, the page states today's behaviour and cites the issue.
- RED FIRST AND MUTANTS. Without the 13 pages both floors fail at 15 of 28; with the floor removed (M1), the new assertion fails, reporting 13 of 28 answering with the stub.
- REVIEW. vc approved v2 after one fix: fullcycle.md's --dry-run paragraph said the dry run writes no log, and a sealed lone build.run writes one; both halves were driven before the page was rewritten.
- THE SUITE. On ea5fdd1 plus 0115, the fifteen files that read a page or run help: 1..522, 522 ok, 0 not ok, rc 0. It landed through the gate, and the commit holds the build's bytes on all 14 paths.
